source: Paladini et al. (2018), Nature 553, 310, the calibrated VLTI/PIONIER visibilities they imaged from (https://doi.org/10.1038/nature25001)

fit.data: Paladini et al.'s (2018) calibrated VLTI/PIONIER visibilities, inside the first lobe

band: VLTI/PIONIER H band (1.5-1.8 um); not a visible band

alpha.cell: alpha 1.29 (1.18 to 1.39 with the diameter refitted), limb-darkened diameter 21.38 mas, reduced chi-squared 5.97 over the 341 squared visibilities shorter than the first null of the 18.17 mas uniform disc; the uncertainty is the larger side

note: No paper publishes a limb law for this star: Paladini et al. fit a uniform disc. The first lobe is where the whole disc dominates; past it the convection cells do, and a power law fitted to every baseline gives 0.42 with the diameter 18.94 mas, a law of the cells rather than of the limb. The sphere keeps the 18.17 mas uniform-disc size the image is cast on.
